analysis:
PORTFOLIO REVIEW: Six positions at 81% deployed — already above the 3-5 concentrated target. Two positions are absent from the screened candidate list, which is a yellow flag requiring explicit attention.

LII (-7.29%, $533.58 vs $575.57 avg): Not present in the screened candidates, suggesting it may have failed the trend filter this cycle. A -7.3% drawdown from entry is substantial and momentum is clearly negative. Original stop was presumably set near 10-15% below entry (~$489). While the stop has not been triggered, the thesis warrants review — Lennox's HVAC demand cycle appears to be rolling over alongside mixed housing data. If price does not stabilize and reclaim $550 in the coming 2 weeks, the position should be exited at market to protect remaining capital. Thesis-break risk is elevated.

CI (-4.14%, $283.94 vs $296.21 avg): Also absent from screened candidates. Cigna faces persistent Medicare Advantage pressure and regulatory uncertainty around pharmacy benefits. At -4.1%, the loss is manageable, but with no trend confirmation and sector headwinds, the risk/reward is asymmetric to the downside. Watch closely; if it fails to recover above $290, consider exiting.

A, AMP, FDS, WDAY: All appear in the screened candidate list with basing uptrends. Theses intact — hold with existing stops.

MARKET REGIME: SPY is mixed — barely below SMA50 but with a positive 20d slope. Not a fully bearish or bullish environment. With Sortino at -4.15, recent volatility has been predominantly downside. This argues for restraint on new additions.

NEW TRADE: With only $13,472 of headroom, one carefully sized position is feasible. VEEV (Veeva Systems) offers the best combination of quality fundamentals (PEG 0.88, fortress balance sheet at D/E 1.41, $1.3B FCF, 16.3% revenue growth) with a genuine basing pattern at 30% of 52-week range, positive SMA50 slope, and 43 days before earnings — enough runway to develop. This is the single actionable setup worth initiating at reduced size given capacity constraints.

trades.entry_strategy: Limit order at $195.00 or better; accept fill up to $199 if market continues to show strength. Prefer entry on any intraday pullback toward the SMA50 zone. Do not chase above $200.
trades.rationale: FUNDAMENTAL: Veeva is a dominant vertical-SaaS platform in life sciences (CRM, Vault, Data Cloud) with a near-monopolistic position in pharma. Fortress balance sheet — D/E of just 1.41, effectively debt-free for a software company. FCF of $1.3B on $32B market cap yields ~4% FCF yield. Forward P/E 19.67 and PEG 0.88 imply the market is pricing in modest growth when the business is delivering 16.3% revenue growth with 30.9% operating margins. EPS revisions modestly positive. TECHNICAL: Stock basing at the lower 30% of its 52-week range ($151-$306), establishing a floor after a deep correction. SMA50 slope turned positive (+4.9%), price reclaimed the SMA50 (+14.7% above it, but this reflects the basing rally not a late-stage extension since absolute price is still 5.3% below SMA200). Earnings 43 days out (Sep 2) provides adequate time to work before catalyst risk. Pattern resembles Stage 1-to-2 transition.
trades.exit_plan: Hard stop at $180.50 (2x ATR below entry, ~7.4%). Time stop: reassess fully if no progress toward $215 within 6 weeks. Thesis-break exits: (1) revenue growth decelerates below 12% at September earnings; (2) major pharma customer defection announced; (3) stock fails to hold SMA50 on a weekly close. Trim 30-50% of position if stock reaches $238 or gets extended more than 18% above SMA50 before earnings. Do not hold through September earnings at full size — reduce to half if the position has not hit target by late August.
